family: CEOS CESCOR optical paths and physical hexapoles
title: Advancing the Hexapole Cs-Corrector for the Scanning Transmission Electron Microscope
owner: Microscopy Society of America; author copy hosted by CEOS GmbH
supported_facts: The paper explicitly lists the corrector's DPH/DP/BTlt/BSh alignment functions.
The text on p443 explicitly states that HP1/HP2 each have six ferromagnetic pole pins made of nickel-iron alloy.
Fig. 3 is a frontal photograph of the physical device, not a mechanical section; pole pieces, coils and yoke are visible, and the caption explicitly states that a liner tube exists but is not shown.
This confirms the physical hexapole structural family of the main CESCOR HPs; absence of polecount in TOML must not be interpreted as a plain tube without internal structure.
unsupported_claims: The optical diagram does not give details of the DPH winding host.
The 8 mm bore, 30 mm pole length and 152 mm yoke outer diameter belong to its 2006 design, not this project's current dimensions; they must not be conflated as matching.
rights_note: Rights to the original remain with their respective holders; public access does not imply an open license. Retained only for traceable reference in this project, with no claim that the original is this project's own work.
assembly_comparison_rule: This source supports structural/functional categories; the instrument's axial/radial values remain governed by the original TOML. Additional structures or replacement dimensions require separate evidence and must not be inferred from schematic proportions.
visual_review: 2026-10-11: PDF page 3 Fig.3 visually inspected; real six-pole assembly photograph, not a mechanical cross-section.
